Rebecca / Brimley team,

Thanks for sharing the draft Order Form earlier. We reviewed the redlines and flagged two areas where we need quick alignment so we can keep the demo environment and pilot timeline intact:

1) Training / feedback license carve-out — Brimley has proposed a broad grant that would allow using customer content for model training without restriction. We typically ask for either an explicit opt-in or a scoped telemetry exception: aggregated telemetry + quality metrics only, no persistent inclusion of customer PII or customer data into public training sets.

2) Deployment restrictions / hosted vs private — your redline seems to require us to host in Brimley-managed VPC for any data used in retraining. We are fine with private deployments for production workloads, but need the Order Form to reflect the operational reality: hosted API (SaaS) usage continues to be covered under our standard data handling & no-training default unless customer elects a separate training agreement.

Attached: a short proposed clause that narrows the training license and an annotated PDF of your redlines. Can you confirm Brimley’s stance on:
- Whether procurement wants a blanket training prohibition, or an exception for aggregated telemetry/ops metrics;
- Whether the Order Form should explicitly list which deployment modes trigger additional terms (Private/VPC vs Hosted).

If you prefer, we can run a 20-minute call today. We’d like to avoid legal stalls before the pilot kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman

Hi Naomi — thanks for the quick note and for the attachments. We discussed internally and uploaded our consolidated redlines (see attached PDF). A few items for clarification from our side:

- Brimley’s position is currently a default: no training of models on customer content unless explicitly agreed. That said, procurement is asking us to grant Redwood a limited right to use anonymized operational telemetry for performance improvements (e.g., latency, error rates, pattern detection). Is that something you can accept if we restrict it to aggregated metrics and prohibit any data reconstruction?

- On deployments: procurement proposed language that requires any model retraining or customer-data-derived model artifacts be done in a Brimley-controlled environment. We’re open to a middle path where training on customer-owned datasets happens only under a separate Professional Services or Private Deployment SOW.

Can you (or your legal contact) provide suggested wording for: 1) the operational telemetry exception; and 2) a short fallback clause that says retraining on customer data requires a separate Order Form / SOW?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

Rebecca Shaw
Director, Contracts & Privacy | Brimley Health

Naomi / team — thanks for flagging. I drafted two short proposals (see below) that we can push back with. I also attached a plain-text snippet for quick copy/paste into the Order Form.

Option A (Recommended — pragmatic):
"Customer Data; Training Exclusion. Except as expressly set forth in a separate written Training Statement of Work (\"Training SOW\"), Redwood will not use Customer Data to improve or train its foundation models. Redwood may process aggregated, de‑identified operational telemetry (e.g., request latencies, error rates, token throughput) for the sole purpose of improving service performance and reliability, provided such telemetry cannot be used to reconstruct Customer Data or identify Customer."

Option B (Conservative — customer control):
"No Training Without SOW. Redwood shall not use Customer Data for any model training, tuning, or improvement unless Customer executes a separate Training SOW specifying scope, location, and security controls. All model retraining using Customer Data shall occur only within environments explicitly designated by Customer (for example, Customer VPC or Customer‑controlled on‑premises systems)."

Order Form mapping suggestion:
- Add a checkbox in the Order Form: "Allow operational telemetry (aggregated, de‑identified) for service improvements" (default: unchecked).
- Add a reference line under 'Additional Services' that points to 'Training SOW required for any Customer Data retraining' with a link to the Training SOW template.

Attachments: proposed_training_clause_20261115.txt (plain text above)

Questions for Naomi/Vanessa/Marissa:
- Do we want to keep the default unchecked (i.e., no telemetry unless customer opts in)? That would match our conservative posture but may slow conversions.
- If we propose default = unchecked, do we want to offer a pilot-specific temporary opt-in UI flow to avoid blocking Brimley’s pilot next week?

I suggest we send Option A with the Order Form mapping and offer the pilot-specific temporary opt-in as an implementation compromise.

—Karthik
